title: Evaluation of a newly developed physical and occupational therapy assessment for patients in neurological-neurosurgical early rehabilitation
summary:
Due to the further development of emergency medicine, more and more patients are surviving illnesses and injuries that would have led to death 20 years ago. Because of this fact, a new form of neurological rehabilitation has become established in Germany: The neurological-neurosurgical early rehabilitation (NNER) (phase B) in which very severely affected patients are treated after neurological illness. An important role in this rehabilitation phase is played, among other things, by physiotherapy and occupational therapy, which mainly work on the patients' sensory motor skills (i.e. sensing and moving). In order to assess whether the respective treatments are goal-oriented, a regular and standardised assessment should take place in both professions. Although a large number of measurement procedures exist that allow conclusions to be drawn about the sensorimotor abilities of neurological patients, there is as yet no assessment that explicitly allows a statement to be made about the sensorimotor abilities of severely affected phase B patients. 
For this reason, a sensorimotor assessment (SeMo) was and is being developed at the Schmieder Kliniken Allensbach for both physiotherapy and occupational therapy. 

The aim of the study presented here, is to evaluate this newly developed assessment. 

The research hypotheses are:  
1.) The developed assessment is feasible in practical implementation. 
2.) The assessment shows good values in the areas of reliability, validity and responsiveness.

The study is divided into several sub-studies: 
1.) Study to test the feasibility of SeMo physiotherapy
Included in this study are 30 patients who have not yet been treated for more than 48 hours in Phase B of the Schmieder Kliniken. The developed assessment will be carried out with the patients on three consecutive weekdays. The aim is to check whether the assessment is feasible with the patients of phase B and whether there is still a need for modification. 

2.) Study to test the quality criteria of SeMo-physiotherapy
Included in this study will be 50 patients who have not been treated for more than 48 hours in phase B of the Schmieder Kliniken. The assessment will be carried out on three consecutive workdays by two different testers. This is to provide a statement about the reliability of the measuring instrument. 
Four weeks after admission and then again before discharge or transfer to another phase, the assessment is carried out again by a tester within three days. 
In order to obtain a statement about the validity of the measurement instrument, additional, already standardised assessments are also carried out with the test persons. These include the Barthel Index, the Early Rehabilitation Barthel Index, the Coma Remission Scale, the sensorimotor part of the Early Functional Ability Scale, the Trunk Control Test, the Trunk Impairment Scale, the Functional Ambulation Categories and the ICU Mobility Index.
  
3.) Study to test the feasibility of SeMo-occupational therapy
Background and procedure are identical to sub-study 1. However, the feasibility of SeMo-occupational therapy is tested here.   

4.) Study to test the quality criteria of SeMo-occupational therapy
A total of 50 patients who have been treated in Phase B at the Schmieder Clinics in Allensbach and Heidelberg for no longer than three working days will be included in this study. The assessment is conducted on two to three consecutive working days by two different testers. This is intended to allow conclusions to be drawn about reliability, i.e., the consistency of the measurement instrument.
Four weeks and eight weeks after admission, the assessment is repeated within two days by one tester. This is intended, among other things, to provide information about the responsiveness of the assessment.
To make a statement about validity, i.e., the accuracy of the measurement instrument, additional already standardized assessments are also collected. These include the Barthel Index, the Early Rehabilitation Index, the Functional Independence Measure, the Glasgow Coma Scale, the Montreal Cognitive Assessment, the sensory section of the Fugl-Meyer Assessment (upper extremity), the section assessing passive range of motion of the Fugl-Meyer Assessment (upper extremity), the muscle function test for the upper extremity, and the Box and Block Test.
At the time of discharge/transfer, the Barthel Index, the Early Rehabilitation Index, the Functional Independence Measure, the Glasgow Coma Scale, and the Montreal Cognitive Assessment are recorded again. Furthermore, the type of transfer (next rehabilitation phase, discharge home, or transfer to a nursing home) is documented.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.) Barthel index < 30 points 
2.) Consent to participate by patients themselves or by caregivers 
3.) Patient has not been admitted to early rehabilitation for more than 48 hours/ three working days (SeMo-OT) at the time of inclusion in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
1.) Barthel index > 30 points
2.) Lack of consent to participation by patients themselves or by caregivers
